slot.subtopic: Mean free path / mean free time
slot.brief: Multiple-statement MCQ on mean free path and mean free time: dependence on number density and molecular diameter, behaviour with temperature at constant pressure vs constant volume — pick the correct combination.

stem: For a dilute ideal gas of fixed-diameter hard-sphere molecules, let $n$ be number density, $\lambda$ mean free path and $\tau=\lambda/\bar v$ mean free time. For a fixed amount of gas, which statements are correct? (i) $\lambda\propto\dfrac{1}{nd^2}$. (ii) At constant pressure, $\lambda\propto T$. (iii) At constant volume, $\tau\propto T^{-1/2}$. (iv) At constant pressure, $\tau$ is independent of $T$.

verdicts.working: For hard spheres, λ = 1/(√2πnd²). At constant pressure, n ∝ T, so λ ∝ T. Since v̄ ∝ √T, at constant volume τ ∝ T⁻¹ᐟ², while at constant pressure τ ∝ √T. Thus (i), (ii), and (iii) are correct.

working:
$\lambda=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}\pi d^2n}$; $\tau\propto\dfrac{1}{nd^2\sqrt{T}}$; constant $P$: $n\propto T^{-1}\Rightarrow\lambda\propto T,\ \tau\propto T^{1/2}$; constant $V$: $n=\text{constant}\Rightarrow\tau\propto T^{-1/2}$.

Independent check: For hard spheres, λ = 1/(√2πnd²). At constant pressure, n ∝ T, so λ ∝ T. Since v̄ ∝ √T, at constant volume τ ∝ T⁻¹ᐟ², while at constant pressure τ ∝ √T. Thus (i), (ii), and (iii) are correct.
solution:
For hard spheres, $
$$\lambda=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}\pi nd^2},\qquad \tau=\frac{\lambda}{\bar v}\propto\frac{1}{n\sqrt T}.\u000a$$At constant pressure, $$n\propto T^{-1}$$, hence $$\lambda\propto T$$ and $$\tau\propto T^{1/2}$$; at constant volume, $n$ is constant, so $$\tau\propto$ T^{-1/2}$. Thus (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct.
